newsitem.title: KENYA: Police move in to break up protests in Nairobi.
newsitem.headline: Police move in to break up protests in Nairobi.

text.p: Riot police armed with batons moved into a park in Nairobi's city centre on Monday to break up an open air meeting by hundreds of supporters of opposition-backed groups demanding constitutional reforms, witnesses said.
The police, wearing helmets and carrying shields, chased protesters across Uhuru park, breaking up a brief meeting and sending hundreds of others running through the city's streets.
Demonstrators initially sat down in the centre of the park in defiance as police on foot and on horses moved in. But the group got to its feet and ran as policemen came within striking distance.
On the northern outskirts of the capital, witnesses said students set tyres ablaze in the road and pelted cars with stones at Uthiru. There were no immediate reports of casualties.

Opposition-backed groups demanding constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections this year had vowed to organise rallies across the country on Monday. Police said the meetings would be illegal and would be broken up.
